title: Darren Waller agrees to one-year deal with Carolina Panthers: Source
author: Joseph Person
content:
The Carolina Panthers and tight end Darren Waller have agreed to a one-year free-agent deal, a league source confirmed to The Athletic on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak about a player’s contract. Terms of the deal were not disclosed.

The deal adds another chapter to what has been an up-and-down career for Waller, who was ranked No. 88 on The Athletic’s Top 150 free agents list this offseason and ninth among tight ends, but went unsigned through the opening weeks of training camp.

The 33-year-old played in nine games for the Miami Dolphins last season after coming out of a one-year retirement and being acquired in a trade from the New York Giants. He made three starts. Waller’s six receiving touchdowns were tied with Jaylen Waddle for the team lead and marked the second most in a single season in his career. He had 283 yards on 24 receptions.

Waller was largely a disappointment during his one season with the Giants after being acquired from the Las Vegas Raiders for a third-round pick in 2023. Injuries limited him to 12 games, and he finished with 552 receiving yards and one touchdown. He retired ahead of the 2024 season before returning a year later.

For a brief stretch with the Raiders, he was one of the best tight ends in football. He had back-to-back seasons of more than 1,100 receiving yards, punctuated in 2020 by a Pro Bowl campaign in which he had 107 catches for 1,196 yards and nine touchdowns — all career highs.

A sixth-round pick in 2015 by the Baltimore Ravens, Waller’s career was nearly derailed by substance abuse issues that led to a four-game suspension in 2016 and a season-long suspension in 2017. It wasn’t until he was signed off the Ravens’ practice squad by the then-Oakland Raiders in 2018 that he got back on an active roster.

The Panthers have lacked a game-changing tight end since Greg Olsen left for Seattle after the 2019 season. So it’s been a while. The current group, which includes Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans and Ja’Tavion Sanders, isn’t devoid of talent. But no one in that tight end room will keep defensive coordinators up at night.

In his prime, Waller was one of the league’s premier pass-catching tight ends, with back-to-back 1,100-yard receiving seasons in 2019 and ’20. But Waller sat out the 2024 season and had two stints on the injured list (with hip and pec strains) last year.

The Panthers saw firsthand last year how effective Waller can still be, when the tight end caught all five of his targets for 78 yards and a touchdown in Miami’s Week 5 loss to Carolina. — Joseph Person, Panthers writer

The Panthers are big on adding competition at every position, and Waller at a minimum does that. He was with the Miami Dolphins last year with Darrell Bevell, who came to Carolina in the offseason as an offensive specialist. Waller caught only 24 passes in nine games for the Dolphins, but six went for touchdowns.

Adding Waller feels like a shot across the bow at the Panthers’ younger tight ends in particular. Sanders, a fourth-round pick in 2024, is a downfield receiving threat who had slipped to third on the depth chart behind Tremble and Evans. If Waller stays healthy, he’ll quickly take over that role.  — Person, Panthers writer
